15986181_b33b6296.text: The mammillothalamic tract is a well-organized projection system described in different mammals and innervating three anterior thalamic nuclei (anteromedial, anteroventral and anterodorsal)
15986181_b33b6296.section: Developmental origin and maturation of excitatory ATN neurons

15986181_54a8a5db.text: .At E20-21 the MTh grows into the ventromedial region of the anterior thalamic nuclei (Figures 4D, 6B). This fact is in agreement with the evidence that the different nuclear components of the anterior thalamus can be distinguished in the rat at E21 (Coggeshall, 1964). Thus the MBO innervation of the anterior thalamic nuclei develops from late prenatal stages (innervation of the ipsilateral anteromedial nucleus at E20-21). On P1-P2, MBO axons start to innervate the ipsilateral anteroventral thalamic nucleus
15986181_54a8a5db.section: Developmental origin and maturation of excitatory ATN neurons

15986181_a8d2bba9.text: .On P1-P2, MBO axons start to innervate the ipsilateral anteroventral thalamic nucleus. At the same time, a separate bundle courses forward in the direction of the anterodorsal thalamic nuclei ipsi-and contralaterally forming the thalamic decussation. At P3-P4, labeled fibers of the MTh filled the whole volume of the anteroventral and began to form the terminal network in the anterodorsal thalamic nuclei. The terminal network consisted of fine beaded nervous processes tightly surrounding all neurons inside the anterior thalamic nuclei (Figure 6C). Immunocytochemical visualization of synapsin, a marker of functioning brain synapses (Melloni et al., 1994)(Castejón et al., 2004), revealed immunolabeling in the anterior thalamic nuclei as small dots in the neuropil around neurons and density of their distribution correlated with density of the DiI labeled terminal network in each nucleus (Alpeeva et al., 2009). By P5-P6 and P10 the density of fluorescent Mth terminal arborizations in all three nuclei of the anterior thalamus has grown significantly (Figure 6D)
15986181_a8d2bba9.section: Developmental origin and maturation of excitatory ATN neurons

15986181_70cb22a2.text: .Separate labeling of the medial mammillary nucleus or lateral mammillary nucleus with little spread outside revealed that the axons from the lateral MBO innervate both anterodorsal thalamic nuclei (left and right) and the axons from the medial MBO innervated anteroventral and anteromedial thalamic nuclei on the side of DiI insertion. This is in agreement with the data obtained in adult rat (Watanabe et al., 1980)(Seki et al., 1984)(Hayakawa et al., 1989)(Hatton, 1990)(Gonzalo-Ruiz et al., 1998).
